title: Handshake serialization failure causing token drip on Dedicated clusters — Customer escalation
creator: Diego Martinez
description: High-severity customer escalation from a Dedicated deployment: multiple customers on Dedicated clusters reported sustained tokens/sec drop and TTFT spikes starting 2026-03-11 23:00 UTC. Problem affects mixed-precision quantized models served on dedicated pools with regional heavy networking (IB) jitter. Initial traces show first-token and early-token emission delays (token drip) rather than full request failures. This ticket tracks the triage, emergency mitigation, root cause, and permanent fix rollout.
reproduction_steps: 1) Provision a Dedicated pool with rwd-open-13b-q8 variant pinned to runtime-1.21 image
2) Replay customer request traces (bucket:dedicated-us-east-requests_20260311) with same batching profile and concurrency
3) Observe first-token RTT distribution and tokens/sec metric (Grafana panel: Dedicated / per-model / tokens/sec)
4) Run binary with --enable-fast-serialization and compare to stable serial path to reproduce handshake mismatch that produces 50-200ms drip between first 3 tokens
investigation: Telemetry: Grafana and span traces show repeated handshake re-negotiations between coalescer and model worker during stream-start when mixed-precision kernel is selected. Traces correlate with ~1.5x increase in TTFT and 40-60% loss in tokens/sec for affected buckets. Heap/CPU on workers is stable; NVLink/IB metrics show transient queue delay but not sufficient to explain the magnitude. Root cause hypothesis: a serialization format mismatch introduced in runtime-1.21 where the fast-path kernel emits a compact handshake token header that older deserialization logic treats as partial stream, causing the streaming sender to wait for completion of a second frame; this results in token-level stalls (token drip) for the first N tokens. The issue is amplified for Dedicated pools because of aggressive kernel coalescing and the region-level NIC jitter.
mitigation: Immediate actions executed 2026-03-12: 1) pushed a routing rule to affected clusters to force variant fallback to the stable cast kernel (variant: rwd-open-13b-q8-cast) for customer-tenants with active escalations; 2) enabled hedging for first-token across the Dedicated cluster to trigger the fallback path after 120ms; 3) performed rolling restart of 30% of affected workers to clear mixed state. Result: tokens/sec for escalated customers recovered to ~92% of baseline within 45 minutes and TTFT reduced by ~60% on average. These mitigations are temporary and intended to buy time for a targeted patch.
pr_links: https://github.com/redwood-inference/runtime/pull/3892 - fix: normalize serialization header across kernels (draft)
https://github.com/redwood-inference/runtime/pull/3896 - perf: hedged-first-token controller tunables for dedicated pools
results: Post-mitigation telemetry shows per-customer tokens/sec recovered to 88-96% of baseline depending on request fanout. No data loss observed; error rates unchanged. Customer CSAT updated with interim mitigation and SLA credit offer. Monitoring: increased sampling of first-10-token spans and a new alert when token emission gap > 80ms over 3s window.
